newsitem.title: USA: Clinton lead stays at 3.8 percent in Reuters poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton lead stays at 3.8 percent in Reuters poll.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and Republican Bob Dole both picked up support on Saturday, leaving Clinton's lead unchanged at 3.8 percentage points in the Reuters/Zogby daily tracking poll released on Sunday.

The poll, conducted for Reuters by John Zogby Group International, a polling company in New York state, surveyed 1,200 likely voters between Thursday and Saturday and carried a margin of error of plus or minus three percentage points.
Clinton scored 43.5 percent, Dole polled 39.7 percent, Reform Party candidate Ross Perot was the choice of 7.2 percent and 7.7 percent remained undecided.
Other polls showed Clinton with a wider lead with two days to go until Election Day. But several also showed the race narrowing.

The major change in the Reuters/Zogby poll came in the race for Congress where Republicans have now taken the lead. Asked who they would vote for in their own district, 40.7 percent said they would support Republicans compared to 37.9 percent who backed Democrats.
That represented a two point pickup for the Republicans in the past 24 hours alone and a 1.5 percent drop for the Democrats.

When asked which party they would prefer to see controlling the Congress, 45.6 percent said they wanted Republicans to control the Senate compared to 36.9 percent for the Democrats. For the House of Representatives, 44.9 percent preferred the Republicans and 36.9 percent wanted a Democratic majority.

In the presidential race, both Clinton and Dole picked up 1.1 percentage points in the past 24 hours, partly at the expense of Perot who lost 1.2 points. The number of undecided voters fell by 2.2 points.
